candidates.attacker_control: The 'request_uri' query parameter (GET, AuthorizationEndpoint.buildGet, line 108) or form field (POST, buildPost line 102) reaching the public endpoint /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth. The value is an arbitrary absolute URL fully controlled by the requester; only a plausible existing 'client_id' for an enabled, non-bearer-only OIDC client is needed, and client_id values are public (exposed on the login/authorization page). No authentication, session, or client secret is required.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for any URI/authority checks on request_uri: none in parseRequest, in AuthzEndpointRequestObjectParser, or in OIDCAdvancedConfigWrapper.getRequestObjectRequired (which only enforces parameter presence per configuration). The 'redirect_uri' parameter is separately validated via RedirectUtils, but that code is not applied to 'request_uri'. Checked that 'request' + 'request_uri' together are rejected, and that the fetch is not restricted to the client's configured request-object/JWKS URIs. Checked other HttpClientProvider call sites: JWKS URI, sector_identifier_uri and identity-provider import URL are configuration/admin-controlled values, not anonymous request input. Confirmed the sink is a plain GET with no host allow-list or scheme restriction in DefaultHttpClientFactory.get(). No runtime validation was performed.
candidates.impact: Blind SSRF: the Keycloak server can be coerced into issuing HTTP(S) GETs to arbitrary internal/external endpoints, including loopback, RFC1918 hosts, and cloud metadata addresses, enabling internal service reachability/port probing and unwanted interactions with internal HTTP services (e.g., triggering state-changing GET endpoints or basic-auth-less admin interfaces). The fetched body is not reflected to the attacker (it is parsed as a JWT and errors yield a generic invalid_request page), so confidentiality impact is limited, but the trust-boundary violation (CWE-918) is real and unauthenticated.
candidates.prerequisites: Realm is enabled and the request passes checkSsl (true on HTTPS deployments or realms with SSL 'none/external'). A valid, enabled OIDC client_id must be supplied so checkClient succeeds. The attacker must not supply the 'request' parameter at the same time (both together are rejected at line 51-53). Alternatively, a client configured with request-object-required values only enforces presence, never the URI. No network position inside the server is needed; the server performs the request itself.
candidates.root_cause: AuthorizationEndpointRequestParserProcessor takes the client-supplied 'request_uri' and passes it directly to session.getProvider(HttpClientProvider.class).get(...) (lines 49, 70-75). There is no validation that the URI belongs to the client (no comparison against a registered request-object URI, no host/scheme allow-list, no redirect-utils check). The default HttpClientProvider implementation then performs a plain outbound GET: DefaultHttpClientFactory creates `new HttpGet(uri)` and executes it on the shared client (lines 99-107), so Keycloak issues an HTTP(S) request to any attacker-chosen absolute URL.
candidates.title: Unauthenticated blind SSRF via OIDC 'request_uri' in the authorization endpoint
candidates.trace: AuthorizationEndpoint.buildGet()/buildPost() -> process(params) (AuthorizationEndpoint.java:105-118) -> AuthorizationEndpointRequestParserProcessor.parseRequest (line 42) -> requestUriParam = requestParams.getFirst("request_uri") (line 49) -> else-if branch (line 70) -> session.getProvider(HttpClientProvider.class).get(requestUriParam) (line 71) -> DefaultHttpClientFactory$1.get(String uri) (lines 99-107): new HttpGet(uri); httpClient.execute(request) -> entity.getContent(). The outbound request is performed before any verification of the fetched document; parsing/verification failures at AuthzEndpointRequestObjectParser only produce a generic 400 (catch at lines 80-84), so the fetch is not gated by the doc being a valid/signed JWT.
candidates.unverified: No runtime/exploit execution was performed. The precise reach of the SSRF depends on network topology and firewall rules around the Keycloak host; the fetched response is not returned to the caller (blind). I did not verify whether later upstream versions added a request_uri allow-list, since only this snapshot was inspected.

coverage_summary: Assigned tree: 5,108 files, all visible to the tools (binary-like files unreadable); no files were reported as excluded by name/path. I reviewed OIDC endpoints and request parsing (AuthorizationEndpoint, TokenEndpoint, LogoutEndpoint, request parsers), SAML IdP/broker paths (SamlService, SAMLEndpoint, signature verification utilities), adapter token verification, admin REST resources and fine-grained admin permission evaluators, authenticators (browser/direct-grant/x509/ECP/Docker), action-token framework, JWS/JWE/JWT verification utilities, redirect/URI utilities, LDAP query building, and export/import file handling. The snapshot notably excludes all test sources (*/src/test/**, testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/**) and all FreeMarker templates (*.ftl), so theme/template XSS and test-encoded expected behavior could not be inspected. Review was source-reading only: no builds, tests, scanners, or exploit execution; the relation index was used only for navigation and every cited edge was verified against source text.
limitations: Only a single candidate may be submitted; the SSRF was selected over several other plausible but weaker or intent-dependent leads (ECP disabled-user handling, admin-only URL import SSRF, form_post escaping, action-token replay).
No runtime verification, build, or dynamic test was performed; all conclusions are static source analysis, and the SSRF's practical reach depends on deployment network topology.

The assigned snapshot omits all test sources and FreeMarker templates, so vulnerabilities that live in templates (e.g., login/account themes) or that are only visible through tests are out of scope/uninspected.
Coverage is not exhaustive across 5,108 files; large modules (authentication, authorization services, model layers, adapters, themes JS) were sampled rather than read line-by-line.

The relation index is syntactic/navigational only and was not treated as proof of data flow, reachability, or exploitability; index facts were absent for both the candidate and the main rejected lead.

I could not determine the exact upstream fix commit or CVE associated with this snapshot from the source alone, so the candidate is the strongest issue I could substantiate, not a confirmed match to any particular historical patch.

rejected_leads.lead: SAML ECP HTTP Basic authenticator accepts disabled users: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/saml/profile/ecp/authenticator/HttpBasicAuthenticator.java (lines 41-46, 61-63) branches on user.isEnabled() but its base userDisabledAction() calls userSuccessAction(), and AuthenticationProcessor.validateUser is not re-run at flow completion, so a disabled account with a valid password appears to obtain a session via the ECP flow (and no brute-force/lockout check exists in this path).
rejected_leads.reason: Strong anomaly (contradicts its own isEnabled() guard and sibling authenticators), but I could not establish from the snapshot alone that this is unintended rather than long-standing upstream behavior; exploitation also requires knowing the disabled account's password. Kept as the main alternative lead rather than submittable.

rejected_leads.lead: Admin-only SSRF: IdentityProvidersResource.fetchFromUrl/import path performs session.getProvider(HttpClientProvider.class).get(fromUrl) on the admin-supplied 'fromUrl' (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/IdentityProvidersResource.java lines 137-139).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an authenticated realm-admin with manage-identity-providers; this is largely the intended 'import metadata from URL' feature, so impact/authorization context is much weaker than the unauthenticated request_uri fetch.

rejected_leads.lead: OIDC form_post response mode builds the FORM ACTION from redirectUri without HTML-attribute escaping (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/utils/OIDCRedirectUriBuilder.java lines 143-165); hidden-input values are escaped but the action is not.
rejected_leads.reason: The URI is first validated against client-registered redirect URIs via RedirectUtils; triggering markup injection would require a maliciously registered redirect URI (client configuration access), so it is config-dependent rather than attacker-controlled.

rejected_leads.lead: OIDC request object with alg=none is accepted when the client has no request_object signature algorithm configured (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/endpoints/request/AuthzEndpointRequestObjectParser.java lines 48-70).
rejected_leads.reason: With no signature requirement configured, an unsigned request object carries essentially the same attacker-controlled parameters as the plain query string, so I found no demonstrable privilege or response bypass beyond existing behavior.

rejected_leads.lead: AbstractActionTokenHander.canUseTokenRepeatedly defaults to true (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authentication/actiontoken/AbstractActionTokenHander.java lines 101-104), so handlers that do not override it (e.g., VerifyEmail) are not invalidated after use.
rejected_leads.reason: Could not confirm intended default from the snapshot; the only handlers with security-critical single-use semantics (reset credentials, execute actions) override the method, and the interface javadoc is ambiguous. Rejected as insufficiently evidenced.

summary: Keycloak 4.6.0.Final-SNAPSHOT server snapshot (5,108 files). The strongest source-evidenced issue found is an unauthenticated blind SSRF in the OIDC authorization endpoint: the `request_uri` parameter is fetched server-side via the shared HTTP client without any scheme/host validation or client-side allow-listing. I verified the full path from the public GET/POST handler to the outbound `HttpGet`. Secondary leads (ECP disabled-user behavior, admin-only import-from-URL SSRF, unescaped form_post ACTION) are listed as unconfirmed/rejected. Test sources and FreeMarker templates are absent from the assigned snapshot, limiting coverage of theme/XSS and test-encoded behavior; nothing was executed.
